content.content:
# Audit instructions

This workspace holds one pull request against the Loa framework repository, frozen for evaluation.

- `PR.md` — the PR title and description
- `head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base → head)
- `base/` — every touched file before the change
- `head/` — every touched file after the change

Audit the change as the security auditor for this repository. There is no sprint plan, beads database, implementation report or `grimoires/loa/a2a/` directory here — the PR files above are the entire input; skip any pre-flight step that needs them and do not ask questions.

Write your audit to `audit.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your auditor skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.
====
---
name: audit
description: Security and quality audit of application codebase
role: review
effort: medium
allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, WebFetch, WebSearch, Bash(.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh *), Bash(br sync --import-only), Bash(br sync --flush-only), Bash(br comments add *), Bash(br label add *), Bash(.claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob *)
disallowed-tools:
  - NotebookEdit
capabilities:
  schema_version: 1
  read_files: true
  search_code: true
  write_files: true
  execute_commands:
    allowed:
      - command: ".claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["sync", "--import-only"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["sync", "--flush-only"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["comments", "add", "*"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["label", "add", "*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
        args: ["knob", "*"]
    deny_raw_shell: true
  web_access: true
  user_interaction: false
  agent_spawn: false
  task_management: false
cost-profile: heavy
context: fork
parallel_threshold: 2000
audit_categories: 5
timeout_minutes: 60
zones:
  system:
    path: .claude
    permission: none
  state:
    paths: [grimoires/loa, .beads]
    permission: read-write
  app:
    paths: [src, lib, app]
    permission: read
inputs:
  # ICM Layer-2 advisory manifest; a missing path WARNs.
  - path: grimoires/loa/known-failures.md
    why: Context-Intake Discipline — read first
  - path: .claude/rules/zone-system.md
    why: System-Zone boundary the audit enforces
---

<input_guardrails>
<!-- @skill-include: start input_guardrails | hash:957e7f01 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/input_guardrails.md -->
## Pre-Execution Guardrails (mechanized)

Run only if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob guardrails.input.enabled false` prints `true`
and env `LOA_GUARDRAILS_ENABLED` is not `false`: write the prompt/args to a temp file (Write tool), then run
`.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill auditing-security --mode ${LOA_RUN_MODE:-interactive} --file <temp-file>`

| Outcome | Action |
|---------|--------|
| JSON `action: "BLOCK"` | HALT; report the script's `reason` to the user |
| JSON `action: "PROCEED"` or `"WARN"` | Continue (the script logs) |
| Script missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output | Continue (fail-open) |

Never pass prompt text as a bash argv (quote-blindness FP class) — always via `--file`.
<!-- @skill-include: end input_guardrails -->
</input_guardrails>

# Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor

<objective>
Audit code, architecture, infrastructure or sprint implementations for security and quality; produce prioritized findings with actionable remediation at the output path for the audit type.
</objective>

<zone_constraints>
## Zone Constraints

Three-Zone Model per CLAUDE.loa.md: `.claude/` system = never edit (use `.claude/overrides/` or `.loa.config.yaml`); `grimoires/loa/`, `.beads/` state = read/write; this skill's app zone (`src/`, `lib/`, `app/`) = **Read-only**.

Scope: app-zone files less the `.reviewignore` patterns (read it); `.claude/`, `grimoires/`, `.beads/` and `.run/` are excluded unless `--no-reviewignore` is passed.
</zone_constraints>

<integrity_precheck>
<!-- @skill-include: start integrity_precheck | hash:47b71a70 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/integrity_precheck.md -->
## Integrity Pre-Check (MANDATORY)

Before ANY operation, verify System Zone integrity:

1. Check config: read `integrity_enforcement` in `.loa.config.yaml`
2. If `strict` and drift detected -> **HALT** and report
3. If `warn` -> Log warning and proceed with caution
<!-- @skill-include: end integrity_precheck -->
</integrity_precheck>

<factual_grounding>
<!-- @skill-include: start factual_grounding | hash:edec7c58 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/factual_grounding.md -->
## Factual Grounding (MANDATORY)

Before ANY synthesis, planning, or recommendation:

1. **Extract quotes**: Pull word-for-word text from source files
2. **Cite explicitly**: `"[exact quote]" (file.md:L45)`
3. **Flag assumptions**: Prefix ungrounded claims with `[ASSUMPTION]`

**Grounded Example:**
```
The SDD specifies "PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector extension" (sdd.md:L123)
```

**Ungrounded Example:**
```
[ASSUMPTION] The database likely needs connection pooling
```
<!-- @skill-include: end factual_grounding -->
</factual_grounding>

<context_discipline>
<!-- @skill-include: start context_discipline | hash:8b81d75a | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/context_discipline.md -->
## Context Discipline

Class: `.run/context-class` (`long` default; `standard` via `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=standard` or a
≤200K model). `.claude/protocols/tool-result-clearing.md` — long 20K/50K/30K/150K, standard 2K/5K/3K/15K (single /
accumulated / full file / session) → extract ≤10 files, ≤20 words, file:line to NOTES.md; reason
from it. Big files: `notes-guard.sh read --file F --section <H>` / `--index` first. Start: NOTES.md
"Session Continuity"; end / pre-compaction: update it.
<!-- @skill-include: end context_discipline -->
</context_discipline>

<trajectory_logging>
<!-- @skill-include: start trajectory_logging | hash:e809010f | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/trajectory_logging.md -->
## Trajectory Logging

Log each significant step to `grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory/{agent}-{date}.jsonl`:

```json
{"timestamp": "...", "agent": "...", "action": "...", "reasoning": "...", "grounding": {...}}
```
<!-- @skill-include: end trajectory_logging -->
</trajectory_logging>

<grounding_requirements>
Read the actual implementation (never documentation alone) and cross-reference the technical-debt registry if one exists. Every finding cites the CWE/OWASP/CVE it violates with an absolute URL (not just the name) and quotes the vulnerable code inline. Where purpose or trust context (internal vs external) is unclear, state the assumption; say "Unable to assess" for obfuscated or inaccessible code and record scope limits in the report.
</grounding_requirements>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Splitting (large scopes)

When splitting, use 5 parallel Explore agents — one per category (Security / Architecture / Code Quality / DevOps / Blockchain-Crypto) — each scoped to its category's files and returning findings with severity, file:line, and remediation (per-category file globs and prompts: see `resources/PARALLEL-SPLIT.md`). Consolidate: deduplicate overlaps, sort CRITICAL → LOW, take the overall risk from the highest severity present.
</parallel_execution>

<rubric_scoring>
## Rubric-Based Scoring

Score each dimension 1–5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md` (Security weighted highest; Blockchain when applicable), recording the findings that justify each score.
</rubric_scoring>

<structured_output>
## Structured JSONL Output

Alongside the markdown report, write machine-parseable findings to `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl` per `resources/OUTPUT-SCHEMA.md` (the schema, each `reasoning_trace`, the closing summary record).
</structured_output>

<communication_style>
Be direct and specific, with evidence: "Line 47: user input passed unsanitized to eval(). Critical RCE. OWASP A03." — never "the code has security issues". Document blast radius, prioritize by exploitability and impact, suggest pragmatic fixes, and never defer a critical issue.
</communication_style>

<documentation_audit>
## Documentation Audit

For sprint audits, confirm each task has a documentation-coherence report (Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-task-*.md`; sprint level: `documentation-coherence-sprint-*.md`) or was manually verified — checks and red-flag tables: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation. Blockers: an unverified missing report; uncommented security-critical code; a CHANGELOG omitting security changes; secrets or internal URLs in docs or comments; auth/crypto changes without security documentation; API changes that don't match the endpoint docs.
</documentation_audit>

<checklists>
Complete checklists for the five categories (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps, Blockchain/Crypto): `resources/REFERENCE.md`. Immediate CRITICAL red flags: private keys in code, SQL via string concatenation, user input to eval(), empty catch blocks on security code, hardcoded secrets.
</checklists>

<beads_workflow>
With `br` installed: `resources/BEADS-WORKFLOW.md` (sync, the audit comment, the `security*` labels, a discovered vulnerability).
</beads_workflow>

<retrospective_postlude>
<!-- @skill-include: start retrospective_postlude | hash:53d44248 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md -->
After the main skill logic, if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled`
prints `true` (and `invisible_retrospective.skills` does not disable this skill), silently run the
learning-signal scan per `.claude/skills/continuous-learning/SKILL.md` and its
`resources/RETROSPECTIVE.md` (quality gates, sanitization, trajectory logging). Never when the
active skill is continuous-learning itself.
<!-- @skill-include: end retrospective_postlude -->
</retrospective_postlude>

## Provenance

Cross-references removed from rule text: review-scope filtering (#303), dissenter anchoring-bias rationale and degraded-review marker (FR-2.5, FR-6.4), documentation-audit version tag (v0.19.0).

# Audit instructions

This workspace holds one pull request against the Loa framework repository, frozen for evaluation.

- `PR.md` — the PR title and description
- `head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base → head)
- `base/` — every touched file before the change
- `head/` — every touched file after the change

Audit the change as the security auditor for this repository. There is no sprint plan, beads database, implementation report or `grimoires/loa/a2a/` directory here — the PR files above are the entire input; skip any pre-flight step that needs them and do not ask questions.

Write your audit to `audit.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your auditor skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.
====
---
name: audit
description: Security and quality audit of application codebase
role: review
effort: medium
allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, WebFetch, WebSearch, Bash(.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh *), Bash(br sync --import-only), Bash(br sync --flush-only), Bash(br comments add *), Bash(br label add *), Bash(.claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob *)
disallowed-tools:
  - NotebookEdit
capabilities:
  schema_version: 1
  read_files: true
  search_code: true
  write_files: true
  execute_commands:
    allowed:
      - command: ".claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["sync", "--import-only"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["sync", "--flush-only"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["comments", "add", "*"]
      - command: "br"
        args: ["label", "add", "*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh"
        args: ["*"]
      - command: ".claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
        args: ["knob", "*"]
    deny_raw_shell: true
  web_access: true
  user_interaction: false
  agent_spawn: false
  task_management: false
cost-profile: heavy
context: fork
parallel_threshold: 2000
audit_categories: 5
timeout_minutes: 60
zones:
  system:
    path: .claude
    permission: none
  state:
    paths: [grimoires/loa, .beads]
    permission: read-write
  app:
    paths: [src, lib, app]
    permission: read
inputs:
  # ICM Layer-2 advisory manifest; a missing path WARNs.
  - path: grimoires/loa/known-failures.md
    why: Context-Intake Discipline — read first
  - path: .claude/rules/zone-system.md

# Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor

<objective>
Audit code, architecture, infrastructure or sprint implementations for security and quality; produce prioritized findings with actionable remediation at the output path for the audit type.
</objective>

<zone_constraints>

<integrity_precheck>

## Integrity Pre-Check (MANDATORY)

Before ANY operation, verify System Zone integrity:

<factual_grounding>
<!-- @skill-include: start factual_grounding | hash:edec7c58 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/factual_grounding.md -->
## Factual Grounding (MANDATORY)

Before ANY synthesis, planning, or recommendation:

1. **Extract quotes**: Pull word-for-word text from source files
2. **Cite explicitly**: `"[exact quote]" (file.md:L45)`
3. **Flag assumptions**: Prefix ungrounded claims with `[ASSUMPTION]`

**Grounded Example:**
```
The SDD specifies "PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector extension" (sdd.md:L123)
```

**Ungrounded Example:**
```

```

</factual_grounding>

<context_discipline>

## Context Discipline

accumulated / full file / session) → extract ≤10 files, ≤20 words, file:line to NOTES.md; reason

</context_discipline>

<trajectory_logging>
<!-- @skill-include: start trajectory_logging | hash:e809010f | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/trajectory_logging.md -->
## Trajectory Logging

```json
{"timestamp": "...", "agent": "...", "action": "...", "reasoning": "...", "grounding": {...}}
```
<!-- @skill-include: end trajectory_logging -->
</trajectory_logging>

<grounding_requirements>
Read the actual implementation (never documentation alone) and cross-reference the technical-debt registry if one exists. Every finding cites the CWE/OWASP/CVE it violates with an absolute URL (not just the name) and quotes the vulnerable code inline. Where purpose or trust context (internal vs external) is unclear, state the assumption; say "Unable to assess" for obfuscated or inaccessible code and record scope limits in the report.
</grounding_requirements>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Splitting (large scopes)

When splitting, use 5 parallel Explore agents — one per category (Security / Architecture / Code Quality / DevOps / Blockchain-Crypto) — each scoped to its category's files and returning findings with severity, file:line, and remediation (per-category file globs and prompts: see `resources/PARALLEL-SPLIT.md`). Consolidate: deduplicate overlaps, sort CRITICAL → LOW, take the overall risk from the highest severity present.
</parallel_execution>

<rubric_scoring>
## Rubric-Based Scoring

Score each dimension 1–5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md` (Security weighted highest; Blockchain when applicable), recording the findings that justify each score.
</rubric_scoring>

<structured_output>
## Structured JSONL Output

Alongside the markdown report, write machine-parseable findings to `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl` per `resources/OUTPUT-SCHEMA.md` (the schema, each `reasoning_trace`, the closing summary record).
</structured_output>

<communication_style>
Be direct and specific, with evidence: "Line 47: user input passed unsanitized to eval(). Critical RCE. OWASP A03." — never "the code has security issues". Document blast radius, prioritize by exploitability and impact, suggest pragmatic fixes, and never defer a critical issue.
</communication_style>

<documentation_audit>
## Documentation Audit

For sprint audits, confirm each task has a documentation-coherence report (Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-task-*.md`; sprint level: `documentation-coherence-sprint-*.md`) or was manually verified — checks and red-flag tables: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation. Blockers: an unverified missing report; uncommented security-critical code; a CHANGELOG omitting security changes; secrets or internal URLs in docs or comments; auth/crypto changes without security documentation; API changes that don't match the endpoint docs.
</documentation_audit>

<checklists>
Complete checklists for the five categories (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps, Blockchain/Crypto): `resources/REFERENCE.md`. Immediate CRITICAL red flags: private keys in code, SQL via string concatenation, user input to eval(), empty catch blocks on security code, hardcoded secrets.
</checklists>

<beads_workflow>
With `br` installed: `resources/BEADS-WORKFLOW.md` (sync, the audit comment, the `security*` labels, a discovered vulnerability).
</beads_workflow>

<retrospective_postlude>
<!-- @skill-include: start retrospective_postlude | hash:53d44248 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md -->
After the main skill logic, if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled`
prints `true` (and `invisible_retrospective.skills` does not disable this skill), silently run the
learning-signal scan per `.claude/skills/continuous-learning/SKILL.md` and its
`resources/RETROSPECTIVE.md` (quality gates, sanitization, trajectory logging). Never when the
active skill is continuous-learning itself.
<!-- @skill-include: end retrospective_postlude -->
</retrospective_postlude>

## Provenance

Cross-references removed from rule text: review-scope filtering (#303), dissenter anchoring-bias rationale and degraded-review marker (FR-2.5, FR-6.4), documentation-audit version tag (v0.19.0).

# Sprint Plan

## Sprint 1: Review the pull request in pr/

The change under review is `pr/head.diff` (unified diff, base to head). The files before the change are under `pr/base/`, after it under `pr/head/`; `pr/PR.md` is the pull request description and is the implementation report for this sprint.

### Tasks

- [x] Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff`

### Review scope

The gates review `pr/head.diff` (pass `--diff-file pr/head.diff` to the adversarial review). Cite findings as `head/<path>:<line>` with lines from the `pr/head/` files.

## Success Criteria

review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict
====BRIEF
# Task brief

## Criterion

review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict

## Task

# Task: review a pull request

The directory `pr/` holds one pull request against a repository of shell scripts, tests and documentation, frozen for evaluation. The change: full-size adapters, Bridgebuilder and Flatline — every size decision derives from the resolved catalog entry.

The pull request is laid out as:

- `pr/PR.md` — the title and description
- `pr/head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base to head)
- `pr/base/` — every touched file before the change
- `pr/head/` — every touched file after the change

Review the change as the senior technical reviewer for the repository: find the defects it introduces and decide whether it can merge. Do not change any file under `pr/`.

## Output contract

Write your review to `review.md` at the repository root (a review workflow that also writes its own report files may do so; `review.md` follows this shape regardless):

- one finding per line, in the form `head/<path>:<line> — <description>`, where `<path>` is the file's path under `pr/head/` and `<line>` is a line number in that file;
- a final line that is exactly `Verdict: APPROVED` or `Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`.

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (= `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The PR (cycle-126 sprint-247, 65 files) replaces the single input-ceiling literal with a policy over the
catalog entry (`loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py`: I1 fit, probed/calibrated/derived/observed bounds, a count
endpoint near the bound, self-correction via `.run/ceiling-observed.json`), gives every provider a
catalog-driven output default, drops the implicit 0.7 temperature, adds `anthropic-beta` allowlisting, a
long-context pricing tier, and re-sizes Flatline and Bridgebuilder from the same catalog rows. The design is
sound and well tested where it is tested: the PR's own Python tests pass (163/164 in an overlay tree; the one
failure is caused by this snapshot's newer `.loa.config.yaml`, not the PR) and its bats tests pass (the
failing bats cases are environmental: a `model-adapter.sh` exec bit lost by my copy and a newer loader
WARN line on stderr).

The self-correction arm (D-1.1b) ships with three defects I reproduced against the head code: a plain
requests-per-minute 429 ends the chain, the "unverified" flag of the head entry is inherited by every
fallback hop, and the observed-bound store loses rows under concurrent writers. Bridgebuilder's new default
model is the alias `opus`, which has no row in either budget table, so the default review runs on the
fallback budget (or the raw 200K operator budget, above cheval's 180K probed bound). The dissent voices
added four medium findings I verified (long-context threshold ignores cached tokens; the retry-layer shrink
is lost on the last attempt; the non-Anthropic output default raises the adapter's own refusal line; the
count-vs-heuristic mismatch between gate and adapter).

Test-run caveat: this snapshot's untouched modules are newer than the PR's base, so the overlay used the
snapshot's `loa_cheval/types.py` (a superset of the head's) to import; every finding below was confirmed
by reading the head files or by a repro that imports only head code.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Functionality — the D-1.1b short-circuit catches every 429, not the token-limit class

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2297` — any `RateLimitError` while `_ceiling_unverified` is set ends the invocation (RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED, exit RATE_LIMITED) instead of walking the chain.
**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2297`
**Issue:** The PR's own comment (lines 2298–2301) scopes this arm to "the token-limit class", but `RateLimitError` carries no class in this PR and the code tests only `_ceiling_unverified`. A requests-per-minute 429 (the common shape under load) on a request that proceeded above the probed bound under `LOA_CHEVAL_UNCALIBRATED_CEILING=derived` is treated as a size verdict.
**Why This Matters:** The operator's declared chain is the contract; here the fallback voice is never tried, the call fails with RATE_LIMITED, and a RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED row is appended to the store for a 429 that said nothing about payload size. Reproduced with the PR's e2e harness: `_run(SIX, errors=[RateLimitError("anthropic")])` under the opt-in dispatches once and exits 1 with `classes=['RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED']`; the PR's own `test_429_while_unverified_is_recorded_not_walked_and_never_lowers_the_bound` (`head/.claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_e2e.py:247-251`) pins this behaviour for a classless 429.
**Required Fix:** Mark the 429 in the adapters (`RateLimitError(..., token_limited=...)` from the 429 body: "tokens per minute", "(TPM)", `context_length_exceeded`, or a context-limit message) and short-circuit only when `token_limited` is true; a request-rate 429 walks as it does under the bound. Update the e2e test to use a token-limited 429 and add the request-rate case (walks, no store row).

### 2. Functionality — `_ceiling_unverified` is head-scoped but applied to every fallback hop

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:1843` — the flag is computed once from the head entry's pre-flight and read at `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2256` and `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2297` for every hop of the walk.
**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:1843`, `2256`, `2297`
**Issue:** "Above the probed bound" is a property of a hop's own entry and budget. A fallback that is calibrated (or whose bound exceeds the estimate) runs the same payload verified, yet inherits the head's `unverified`.
**Why This Matters:** Reproduced with the PR's e2e harness (head above its probed bound under the opt-in, fails 503 and walks; fallback `claude-opus-4-8` calibrated at 900K): a plain 429 on the fallback yields `classes=['PROVIDER_OUTAGE', 'RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED']` and writes a `('claude-opus-4-8', 'RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED')` row against the calibrated model; a provider verdict on the same fallback is classed `CEILING_UNVERIFIED_LIMIT` instead of `PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT`. The store and the envelope then misattribute calibration evidence to the wrong entry, and the head's envelope flag (`ceiling_unverified`) becomes indistinguishable from the fallback's state.
**Required Fix:** Compute `_hop_unverified` per hop inside the walk loop (`input_bound(_hop_entry, max_tokens=_hop_budget, observed=..., policy=...)`; unverified iff not calibrated and `_walk_estimate > decision.probed`) and use it at both arms; keep the head's `ceiling_unverified` on the envelope as the pre-flight record only.

### 3. Data loss — `record_observed` has no inter-process lock

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py:279-299` — read → append → `os.replace` with no lock; concurrent writers overwrite each other's rows.
**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py:279-299`
**Issue:** `load_observed(path)` at line 279 and `os.replace(tmp, path)` at line 299 are not serialised across processes. The docstring calls the store "append-only history", and `observed_for` reduces it to the tightest bound.
**Why This Matters:** Flatline dispatches three voices and the adversarial review two voices concurrently against the same provider with the same payload size, so simultaneous provider verdicts are the normal case, not a corner. Repro importing only `head/.../routing/ceiling.py`: 4 forked writers × 25 rows retained 26, 30 and 27 of 100 rows in three trials. A lost PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT row means the bound is not lowered and the next call repeats the paid failure.
**Required Fix:** Hold an exclusive `fcntl.flock` on a sibling lock file (`<store>.lock`, opened `O_NOFOLLOW`, refused when a symlink or not a regular file, per the repo's atomic-write symlink defences) around load → append → replace; keep temp + `os.replace` for lock-free readers. Add a multi-process test (N writers × M rows all retained).

### 4. Regression — Bridgebuilder's new default model has no token budget

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:172` — `DEFAULTS.model` becomes the alias `opus`, which is a key in neither `GENERATED_TOKEN_BUDGETS` (`head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/core/truncation.generated.ts:19-56`, model ids only) nor the hand table.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:172`, `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/scripts/gen-bb-registry.ts:284-292`, `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/personas/quick.md:2`, `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/personas/security.md:2`
**Issue:** The budget lookup is by model id; the previous default `claude-opus-4-7` had a row (160K/8192). `getTokenBudget("opus")` now falls to the `default` row (100K input, 4096 output) and the effective input budget for an unknown id is the raw operator budget, which this PR raises to 200_000 (`config.ts:176`). Verified by loading head's generated table into the truncation module: `opus → {maxInput:100000,maxOutput:4096}`, `effectiveInputBudget(200000,"opus") = 200000`; `tiny` (the quick persona) behaves the same. Bridgebuilder dispatches through cheval (`adapters/cheval-delegate.ts`), whose probed bound for the alias target is 180K.
**Why This Matters:** Under the default configuration a large PR review is built to 200K estimated tokens and preempted by cheval's pre-flight (CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE, exit 7) where it used to be truncated to 160K; a smaller one runs on a 100K/4096 budget instead of 160K/32K. Either way the "every size decision derives from the resolved catalog entry" goal is not met for the default model, and the PR's new `truncation-registry.test.ts` checks concrete ids only.
**Required Fix:** Have `gen-bb-registry.ts` emit the catalog's `aliases:` block as `GENERATED_MODEL_ALIASES` (provider-qualified targets, self-maps dropped) and resolve an alias to its target id before the budget lookup; add a test that `getTokenBudget("opus")` equals the target's row and that `effectiveInputBudget(200000, "opus")` is clamped to it.

---

## Observations

### 1. Pricing (FR-1.9)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/metering/pricing.py:168` — the long-context tier triggers on `input_tokens > threshold` only; `cache_read_tokens` / `cache_creation_tokens` are, per `ledger.create_ledger_entry`'s contract (`head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/metering/ledger.py:133`, "not part of input_tokens"), separate. A prompt-cached run of 150K cached + 100K fresh tokens is billed at the premium by the provider but recorded at base rates, and `long_context` is absent from the row, so `cost-report.sh` does not count it either. Flatline and Bridgebuilder are exactly this workload (cycle-124 FR-4 cache_control). (Dissent DISS-001 / DISS-C-004, verified.)
**Suggestion:** Compare `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens` with the threshold; add a test with cached tokens above the threshold.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/metering/pricing.py:171-175` — the multipliers are applied to the already-floored per-category micro costs and the remainders (`inp_rem`, `cr_rem`, …) are not recomputed. Repro on head: 3 tokens × 1.25 µUSD × 1.5 = 5.625 → head bills 4 (floor(floor(3.75) × 1.5)), exact floor is 5. Small in money, but the remainder accounting that exists to carry sub-micro amounts is silently discarded on the premium path.

The self-correction arm (D-1.1b) ships with three defects I reproduced against the head code: a plain
requests-per-minute 429 ends the chain, the "unverified" flag of the head entry is inherited by every
fallback hop, and the observed-bound store loses rows under concurrent writers. Bridgebuilder's new default
model is the alias `opus`, which has no row in either budget table, so the default review runs on the
fallback budget (or the raw 200K operator budget, above cheval's 180K probed bound). The dissent voices
added four medium findings I verified (long-context threshold ignores cached tokens; the retry-layer shrink
is lost on the last attempt; the non-Anthropic output default raises the adapter's own refusal line; the
count-vs-heuristic mismatch between gate and adapter).

Test-run caveat: this snapshot's untouched modules are newer than the PR's base, so the overlay used the
snapshot's `loa_cheval/types.py` (a superset of the head's) to import; every finding below was confirmed
by reading the head files or by a repro that imports only head code.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Functionality — the D-1.1b short-circuit catches every 429, not the token-limit class

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2297` — any `RateLimitError` while `_ceiling_unverified` is set ends the invocation (RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED, exit RATE_LIMITED) instead of walking the chain.
**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2297`
**Issue:** The PR's own comment (lines 2298–2301) scopes this arm to "the token-limit class", but `RateLimitError` carries no class in this PR and the code tests only `_ceiling_unverified`. A requests-per-minute 429 (the common shape under load) on a request that proceeded above the probed bound under `LOA_CHEVAL_UNCALIBRATED_CEILING=derived` is treated as a size verdict.
**Why This Matters:** The operator's declared chain is the contract; here the fallback voice is never tried, the call fails with RATE_LIMITED, and a RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED row is appended to the store for a 429 that said nothing about payload size. Reproduced with the PR's e2e harness: `_run(SIX, errors=[RateLimitError("anthropic")])` under the opt-in dispatches once and exits 1 with `classes=['RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED']`; the PR's own `test_429_while_unverified_is_recorded_not_walked_and_never_lowers_the_bound` (`head/.claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_e2e.py:247-251`) pins this behaviour for a classless 429.
**Required Fix:** Mark the 429 in the adapters (`RateLimitError(..., token_limited=...)` from the 429 body: "tokens per minute", "(TPM)", `context_length_exceeded`, or a context-limit message) and short-circuit only when `token_limited` is true; a request-rate 429 walks as it does under the bound. Update the e2e test to use a token-limited 429 and add the request-rate case (walks, no store row).

### 2. Functionality — `_ceiling_unverified` is head-scoped but applied to every fallback hop

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:1843` — the flag is computed once from the head entry's pre-flight and read at `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2256` and `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2297` for every hop of the walk.
**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:1843`, `2256`, `2297`
**Issue:** "Above the probed bound" is a property of a hop's own entry and budget. A fallback that is calibrated (or whose bound exceeds the estimate) runs the same payload verified, yet inherits the head's `unverified`.
**Why This Matters:** Reproduced with the PR's e2e harness (head above its probed bound under the opt-in, fails 503 and walks; fallback `claude-opus-4-8` calibrated at 900K): a plain 429 on the fallback yields `classes=['PROVIDER_OUTAGE', 'RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED']` and writes a `('claude-opus-4-8', 'RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED')` row against the calibrated model; a provider verdict on the same fallback is classed `CEILING_UNVERIFIED_LIMIT` instead of `PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT`. The store and the envelope then misattribute calibration evidence to the wrong entry, and the head's envelope flag (`ceiling_unverified`) becomes indistinguishable from the fallback's state.
**Required Fix:** Compute `_hop_unverified` per hop inside the walk loop (`input_bound(_hop_entry, max_tokens=_hop_budget, observed=..., policy=...)`; unverified iff not calibrated and `_walk_estimate > decision.probed`) and use it at both arms; keep the head's `ceiling_unverified` on the envelope as the pre-flight record only.

### 3. Data loss — `record_observed` has no inter-process lock

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py:279-299` — read → append → `os.replace` with no lock; concurrent writers overwrite each other's rows.
**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py:279-299`
**Issue:** `load_observed(path)` at line 279 and `os.replace(tmp, path)` at line 299 are not serialised across processes. The docstring calls the store "append-only history", and `observed_for` reduces it to the tightest bound.
**Why This Matters:** Flatline dispatches three voices and the adversarial review two voices concurrently against the same provider with the same payload size, so simultaneous provider verdicts are the normal case, not a corner. Repro importing only `head/.../routing/ceiling.py`: 4 forked writers × 25 rows retained 26, 30 and 27 of 100 rows in three trials. A lost PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT row means the bound is not lowered and the next call repeats the paid failure.
**Required Fix:** Hold an exclusive `fcntl.flock` on a sibling lock file (`<store>.lock`, opened `O_NOFOLLOW`, refused when a symlink or not a regular file, per the repo's atomic-write symlink defences) around load → append → replace; keep temp + `os.replace` for lock-free readers. Add a multi-process test (N writers × M rows all retained).

### 4. Regression — Bridgebuilder's new default model has no token budget

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:172` — `DEFAULTS.model` becomes the alias `opus`, which is a key in neither `GENERATED_TOKEN_BUDGETS` (`head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/core/truncation.generated.ts:19-56`, model ids only) nor the hand table.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:172`, `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/scripts/gen-bb-registry.ts:284-292`, `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/personas/quick.md:2`, `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/personas/security.md:2`
**Issue:** The budget lookup is by model id; the previous default `claude-opus-4-7` had a row (160K/8192). `getTokenBudget("opus")` now falls to the `default` row (100K input, 4096 output) and the effective input budget for an unknown id is the raw operator budget, which this PR raises to 200_000 (`config.ts:176`). Verified by loading head's generated table into the truncation module: `opus → {maxInput:100000,maxOutput:4096}`, `effectiveInputBudget(200000,"opus") = 200000`; `tiny` (the quick persona) behaves the same. Bridgebuilder dispatches through cheval (`adapters/cheval-delegate.ts`), whose probed bound for the alias target is 180K.
**Why This Matters:** Under the default configuration a large PR review is built to 200K estimated tokens and preempted by cheval's pre-flight (CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE, exit 7) where it used to be truncated to 160K; a smaller one runs on a 100K/4096 budget instead of 160K/32K. Either way the "every size decision derives from the resolved catalog entry" goal is not met for the default model, and the PR's new `truncation-registry.test.ts` checks concrete ids only.
**Required Fix:** Have `gen-bb-registry.ts` emit the catalog's `aliases:` block as `GENERATED_MODEL_ALIASES` (provider-qualified targets, self-maps dropped) and resolve an alias to its target id before the budget lookup; add a test that `getTokenBudget("opus")` equals the target's row and that `effectiveInputBudget(200000, "opus")` is clamped to it.

---

## Observations

### 1. Pricing (FR-1.9)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/metering/pricing.py:168` — the long-context tier triggers on `input_tokens > threshold` only; `cache_read_tokens` / `cache_creation_tokens` are, per `ledger.create_ledger_entry`'s contract (`head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/metering/ledger.py:133`, "not part of input_tokens"), separate. A prompt-cached run of 150K cached + 100K fresh tokens is billed at the premium by the provider but recorded at base rates, and `long_context` is absent from the row, so `cost-report.sh` does not count it either. Flatline and Bridgebuilder are exactly this workload (cycle-124 FR-4 cache_control). (Dissent DISS-001 / DISS-C-004, verified.)
**Suggestion:** Compare `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens` with the threshold; add a test with cached tokens above the threshold.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/metering/pricing.py:171-175` — the multipliers are applied to the already-floored per-category micro costs and the remainders (`inp_rem`, `cr_rem`, …) are not recomputed. Repro on head: 3 tokens × 1.25 µUSD × 1.5 = 5.625 → head bills 4 (floor(floor(3.75) × 1.5)), exact floor is 5. Small in money, but the remainder accounting that exists to carry sub-micro amounts is silently discarded on the premium path.
**Suggestion:** Compute `floor(tokens × rate × multiplier / 1e6)` per category with the multiplier as an exact decimal, and scale the remainder the same way.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/metering/pricing.py:290-295` — `_mult` accepts non-finite values: `float("inf")` and `"1e309"` pass `m > 0`, and `int(inp_cost * inf)` at line 171 raises `OverflowError`. Repro on head: `find_pricing` parses `input_multiplier: .inf` as `inf`; `calculate_total_cost(10, 10, 0, entry)` raises. `budget_hook.post_call` (`head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2210`) runs inside the walk-loop `try`, so the exception lands in the catch-all (`cheval.py:2402-2420`) and a completed, billed answer is reported as API_ERROR. The parser's own docstring promises "a malformed … block means no premium tier".
**Suggestion:** `math.isfinite(m) and m > 0` (and reject booleans) in `_mult`; add the `.inf` / `nan` / `1e309` cases to `test_long_context_pricing.py`.

### 2. Retry layer (D-1.1b)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/retry.py:472-496` — the one-shot shrink does `request = replace(request, max_tokens=room); continue` inside `for attempt in range(max_retries + 1)` and never sets `last_typed_error` / `last_error`. When the context-limit error arrives on the final iteration (always under `retry.max_retries: 0`; otherwise when earlier attempts were spent on 429/503 backoffs) the loop ends without sending the shrunk request, and the post-loop `RetriesExhaustedError` (line 530) carries the previous transient error's text. cheval's `except RetriesExhaustedError` (`head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2338`) walks, so the identical oversize payload reaches the next voice, no observation is recorded, and the exit is CHAIN_EXHAUSTED rather than CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE. (Dissent DISS-002 / DISS-C-001, verified by reading.)
**Suggestion:** Give the shrink its own retry outside the attempt counter (or re-raise the `ProviderContextLimitError` when no attempt remains), and set `last_typed_error`.

### 3. Output defaults vs. the adapter's own window check (FR-1.3 / D-1.4)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/base.py:187-203` with `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2078-2087` — non-Anthropic hops jump from 4096 to `min(16000, max_output_tokens)`, but the walk-loop I1 fit only runs for entries carrying an HTTP ceiling (Anthropic). `enforce_context_window` (`head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/base.py:1007-1024`) then evaluates `estimate + 16000 ≤ 128000` on gpt-5.2 (context 128K, `max_output_tokens: 16000`, no v2/v3 input fields, so no walk-gate line): a 115K prompt that fit before now raises `ContextTooLargeError` and walks. Silent, because the walk-gate threshold did not change. (Dissent DISS-C-002, catalog fields verified.)
**Suggestion:** Apply the I1 fit to every hop with a `context_window` (not only ceiling-bearing entries), or keep 4096 for entries without a ceiling.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:1840-1842` — when the count endpoint runs, `_walk_estimate` becomes the provider count and the I1 fit grants `max_tokens = context_window − count`; the adapter's `enforce_context_window` (`base.py:1019`) still uses `estimate_tokens` (chars/3.5). For prose where the heuristic overcounts (English ≈ 4 chars/token) a request the gate approved near the window (count 130K on a 200K window with 64K requested: fits; heuristic 150K > 200K − 64K) is refused by the adapter and walked. The gate and the adapter now disagree on units. (Dissent DISS-C-003.)
**Suggestion:** Pass the gate's estimate (or the fitted decision) to the adapter, or have `enforce_context_window` accept an override estimate.

### 4. Flatline (FR-1.6)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: low) `head/.claude/scripts/flatline-orchestrator.sh:129`, `936-946`, `1027` — the 64000 voice cap applies regardless of `LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_STREAMING`. cheval's own non-streaming Anthropic default is 16K (`base.py:187-203`) and `_nonstreaming_read_timeout` caps at 600 s (≈ 15K tokens at 25 tok/s); under the kill switch an explicit 64000 is clamped only to the catalog's 128K. The cycle-124 16000 literal was safe on both transports.
**Suggestion:** Cap at the transport default (16000 when the kill switch is set), or let cheval's per-model default decide by passing no `--max-tokens`.

### 5. Hardening and consistency

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2022` — `message_redacted: str(_exc)` and the stderr JSON at lines 2032-2037 are not passed through `sanitize_provider_error_message` at this new exit. The adapter sanitises `_extract_error_message`, so this is defence in depth, but every other `models_failed` writer in the file redacts at the recording site.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/anthropic_adapter.py:82`, `174` — `\d` matches Unicode digits and `re.match` with `$` accepts a trailing newline, so `"context-1m-٢٠٢٥-08-07"` or `"context-1m-2025-08-07\n"` pass the allowlist and fail later in the HTTP client (ValueError / UnicodeEncodeError) instead of as the promised `ConfigError`. Use `[0-9]` and `fullmatch`.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh:806-808` — the model id is spliced into the yq expression text (use `strenv`); at `811-813` the jq `[.observed_input_tokens, …] | min` yields null when a row lacks `observed_input_tokens`, dropping a `provider_limit`-only row, and a `0` row (cheval records `int(_walk_estimate or 0)` when the gate is disabled and the message states no number, `cheval.py:2005`) renders `ceiling: observed -1` while `observed_for` ignores it.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py:159` — the marker `"too many tokens"` also matches Bedrock's throttle text ("Too many tokens, please wait before trying again"). Only 400/413 reach it in the Anthropic adapter today, so no misfire yet; a throttle marker should outrank a context marker before this classifier is reused.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/base.py:998-1003` — `method = "tiktoken"` is reported whenever the module imports, even when `estimate_tokens` fell back to the heuristic (offline `get_encoding`), so the envelope's `estimator.method` can be wrong.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:1888` and `2105-2109` — the operator-visible "max_tokens shrunk" line is an `elif` behind `action == "warn"` (a request both warned and shrunk prints only the warn), and a fallback-hop shrink writes only the envelope field with no stderr line. An explicit `--max-tokens 64000` can be cut to the 4,096 floor silently. (Dissent DISS-C-006.)
- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/anthropic_adapter.py:672-674` — the message probe runs only when `/models` returns exactly 404; a proxy answering 403/405/501 for unknown paths reports a healthy deployment as down. (Dissent DISS-C-005.) Minor because the pre-cycle probe targeted a retired id.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2016` — on a CLI hop the calibrate hint is `--model claude-headless`, which `write_catalog` refuses (no block fields), and the observation is recorded against the CLI entry, which carries no HTTP ceiling.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `SIMPLICITY[shrink]`: `cmd_invoke` grows by ~250 lines; the pre-flight gate branch (`head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:1805-1862`) nests four deep inside an already multi-thousand-line function, and `_calibration_needed_exit` is a 50-line closure over eleven enclosing names. Extract both to module-level helpers taking the state dict; `_tiny_model_id` (`anthropic_adapter.py:639-659`) can be a one-line `min()` over priced entries after the haiku check. net: -40 lines possible.

### 6. Process

- `reviewer.md` (= `pr/PR.md`) is a one-line title and has no `## AC Verification` walkthrough; per the review protocol this alone forces CHANGES_REQUIRED. Please add the per-FR verification (FR-1.1–FR-1.9) with `file:line` evidence.
- No CHANGELOG is present in this snapshot, so the per-task CHANGELOG entry could not be verified. `multi-model-reference.md` and the Bridgebuilder `SKILL.md` were updated.

Two voices answered (`gpt-5.5-pro` primary, `claude-headless` companion, `counted_as: independent_voice`); eight advisory/blocking findings, triaged above:

"""cycle-126 Sprint 1 Task 1.2 (PRD FR-1.1, SDD D-1.1) — `tools/ceiling-probe-live.py
--write-catalog` folds a probe result into the LIVE catalog text: the model's
ceiling, calibration and account limits change; every comment and every other
entry stay byte-identical; a missing block or field is an error, never a guess.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import yaml

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
TOOL = ROOT / "tools" / "ceiling-probe-live.py"
CATALOG = ROOT / ".claude" / "defaults" / "model-config.yaml"


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def tool():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("ceiling_probe_live", TOOL)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules["ceiling_probe_live"] = mod
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return mod


def test_write_catalog_changes_only_the_probed_entry(tool):
    before = CATALOG.read_text()
    after = tool.write_catalog(before, "claude-opus-5", ceiling=640_000, calibrated_at="2026-09-25T00:00:00Z",
                               sample_size=6, tier="4", itpm=2_000_000)
    b, a = yaml.safe_load(before), yaml.safe_load(after)
    entry = a["providers"]["anthropic"]["models"]["claude-opus-5"]
    assert entry["effective_input_ceiling"] == 640_000 and entry["probed_ceiling"] == 180_000
    assert entry["ceiling_calibration"]["source"] == "empirical_probe"

### DISS-001 [MEDIUM] voice=gpt-5.5-pro
anchor: .claude/adapters/cheval.py:cmd_invoke._calibration_needed_exit
The new calibration exit copies the provider-controlled exception text directly into `message_redacted` and the stderr error response. A context-limit response that echoes a credential or sensitive prompt fragment can therefore expose it in diagnostic output. Apply the existing redaction helper before recording or formatting the exception; the added `test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message` exercises this exact case.
REMEDIATION: -

### DISS-C-001 [MEDIUM] voice=claude-headless
anchor: .claude/adapters/cheval.py:_calibration_needed_exit
Numbers parsed out of a provider's HTTP 400/413 error body (`input_tokens`, `limit` via parse_context_limit) are written unvalidated into the persistent `.run/ceiling-observed.json` store and become the input bound for every later invocation of that (provider, model) until an operator recalibrates (test shows observed_for == limit+1 and the next 600K call preempts). There is no sanity check against the catalog entry (e.g. limit must be <= context_window and >= some floor), and when the message states no numbers the code records cheval's own estimate (`_obs = _walk_estimate`) as the observed failure point. Any 400 whose text happens to satisfy is_context_limit_message (a misclassified validation error, a proxy/gateway error page, a compromised or MITM'd endpoint) therefore permanently lowers the bound, and a body claiming `> 1 maximum` blocks the model entirely. cd /workspace; cat > grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/auditor-sprint-feedback.md <<'EOF'
# Sprint 1 Security Audit Feedback

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (= `pr/PR.md`)
**Scope:** `pr/head.diff` (65 files; cycle-126 sprint-247 — full-size adapters, Bridgebuilder and Flatline sized from the resolved catalog entry). Citations are `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers from `pr/head/`.

---

## Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

---

## Executive Summary

The PR replaces the single input-ceiling literal with a policy module (`loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py`) that derives every size decision from the resolved catalog entry, adds a self-correcting observed-bound store (`.run/ceiling-observed.json`) fed by the provider's own context-limit verdicts, an `anthropic-beta` allowlist, a long-context pricing tier, a count-tokens pre-flight and catalog-driven output defaults for every provider, and re-sizes Flatline and Bridgebuilder from the same rows. No secrets, no new network destinations beyond the configured provider endpoint, and the one new data path (`count_tokens`) sends the already context-filtered prompt (`audit_filter_context` runs at `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:1672`, before the request object is built). The System-Zone boundary is respected: the only writer into `.claude/` is the operator-invoked probe tool, by design (FR-1.1).

The security posture problem is in the self-correction arm (D-1.1b). Numbers parsed from a provider's HTTP 400/413 body, and a broad marker list that classifies the body as a "size verdict", are written unvalidated into a persistent store that lowers the model's input bound for every later invocation until an operator recalibrates; the same arm ends the chain on any 429, inherits the head hop's "unverified" state on every fallback hop, and the store itself loses rows under the concurrent writers Flatline and the adversarial review always produce. Bridgebuilder's new default model is an alias no budget table knows. These are availability and correctness defects rather than confidentiality ones, but four of them are HIGH and the one-way rule forces CHANGES_REQUIRED.

Dissent: two voices (gpt-5.5-pro primary, claude-headless companion, `counted_as: independent_voice`, `degraded: false`, `locality: null`). Not a degraded security review. Six findings, all triaged below; one (DISS-C-001) is counted as a finding of my own, three confirm review findings, two are downgraded with the reason stated.

**Security Issues Found:**
| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 4 |
| Medium | 7 |
| Low | 13 |

---

## Critical Security Issues (Must Fix)

None.

---

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

The review tallied four HIGHs; each is confirmed independently below from the head files and counted as my own.

### [HIGH-001] The D-1.1b 429 arm ends the chain on every RateLimitError, not the token-limit class

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2297`
**Issue:** `except RateLimitError as _e: if _ceiling_unverified: return _calibration_needed_exit(... error_class="RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED" ...)`. The comment at 2298-2301 scopes the arm to "the token-limit class", but `RateLimitError` carries no class — the Anthropic adapter raises it bare on any 429 (`head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/anthropic_adapter.py:343`, `:489`) — and the code tests only `_ceiling_unverified`.
**Impact:** Under `LOA_CHEVAL_UNCALIBRATED_CEILING=derived`, a requests-per-minute 429 (the ordinary shape under load) on a request above the probed bound exits RATE_LIMITED without trying the declared fallback, and appends a RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED row for a 429 that said nothing about size. The operator's chain is the availability contract; this arm voids it. `test_429_while_unverified_is_recorded_not_walked_and_never_lowers_the_bound` (`head/.claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_e2e.py:247`) pins the wrong behaviour for a classless 429.
**Fix:** Classify the 429 in the adapter (`RateLimitError(..., token_limited=True)` when the body says tokens-per-minute / TPM / context-limit) and short-circuit only on `token_limited`; a request-rate 429 walks as it does under the bound. Update the e2e test and add the request-rate case.
**Reference:** CWE-754 Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html

### [HIGH-002] `_ceiling_unverified` is computed once from the head entry and applied to every fallback hop

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:1843` (set), `:2256` and `:2297` (read)
**Issue:** `_ceiling_unverified = _preflight_outcome.unverified` is assigned once in the pre-flight branch and never recomputed inside `for _idx, _entry in enumerate(_chain.entries)`. "Above the probed bound" is a property of a hop's own entry and budget.
**Impact:** A calibrated fallback (or one whose bound exceeds the estimate) that returns a provider verdict is classed `CEILING_UNVERIFIED_LIMIT` instead of `PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT`, and a plain 429 on it hits HIGH-001; either way the store row and the envelope attribute calibration evidence to the wrong model, and the self-correction lowers the wrong bound.
**Fix:** Compute `_hop_unverified` per hop in the walk loop from `input_bound(_hop_entry, max_tokens=_hop_budget, observed=..., policy=...)` (unverified iff not calibrated and `_walk_estimate > decision.probed`) and consult it at both arms; keep the head's flag on the envelope as the pre-flight record only.
**Reference:** CWE-706 Use of Incorrectly-Resolved Name or Reference — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/706.html

### [HIGH-003] `record_observed` has no inter-process lock — concurrent writers lose provider verdicts

### [MED-001] Provider-stated numbers and a broad marker list poison the persistent input bound (self-inflicted denial of a model)
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high) — Confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-001); traced independently.
- **File:** `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2004-2010` (`_obs = int(observed) ... else int(_walk_estimate or 0)`; `record_observed(... provider_limit=provider_limit)`), `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py:157-169` (markers), `:182-198` (`parse_context_limit`), `:240-261` (`observed_for`), `:122-123` (`observed - 1` becomes the bound); raise sites `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/anthropic_adapter.py:361-365`, `:503-507`.
- **Issue:** Any HTTP 400/413 whose sanitised text contains one of eleven substrings ("context window", "input length", "maximum context", …) is typed `ProviderContextLimitError`; the numbers the regexes pull from the body are stored as `observed_input_tokens` / `provider_limit` with no plausibility check against the estimate, the catalog `context_window`, or a floor; when the body states no numbers, cheval's own estimate is stored as the observed failure point. `observed_for` then returns the minimum and `input_bound` makes `observed − 1` the bound for every later call to that (provider, model) until `calibrated_at` is set — which needs a paid probe run.
- **Failure scenario:** a 400 that is not a size verdict but mentions "context window" (e.g. a thinking-budget validation error), or a proxy / gateway error page, or an endpoint under `LOA_CHEVAL_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`-style redirection answering `"1 tokens > 1 maximum"`, pins the bound at 0-1 and every subsequent invocation of the `opus` target preempts CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE. A single response both ends the call (not walked) and poisons future ones; recovery is a manual store edit or the probe command.
- **Fix:** Accept a provider number only when `limit` is within `[FLOOR, context_window]` and `input_tokens` is within a band of the estimate (e.g. 0.5×–2×); never store the estimate as "observed" for `PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT`; require a positive classifier (the two regex shapes) before lowering the bound, and treat marker-only matches as walkable 400s. Add a tamper test (`"1 tokens > 1 maximum"` must not change the bound).
- **Reference:** CWE-1284 Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1284.html; CWE-20 — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html
